title: Directional derivative bound from rotation variation
statement: Let $n\ge 0$, let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ have derivative at every $x$ given by the linear functional $L(x)$, and let $C\in[0,\infty]$. Suppose that for every $\theta>0$, the product Gaussian integral of $|f(\cos\theta X+\sin\theta Y)-f(X)|/\theta$ is at most $C$, where $X$ and $Y$ are independent standard Gaussian vectors in $\mathbb R^n$. Then the product Gaussian integral of $|L(X)Y|$ is at most $C$.
hypotheses_covered: The stated rotation difference integral is at most $C$ for every positive $\theta$
replaced: Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$ and $X,Y$ independent with that law. Let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be differentiable everywhere with derivative $L(x)$, and put $|L(x)|_2=\sqrt{\sum_i(L(x)e_i)^2}$, where $e_i$ is the canonical basis. Let $C\in[0,\infty]$. If $\mathbb E(|f(\cos\theta\,X+\sin\theta\,Y)-f(X)|/\theta)\le C$ for every $\theta>0$, then $\mathbb E|L(X)Y|\le C$, with both expectations interpreted as nonnegative extended integrals.
